problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(-2,11,1)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $r\cdot ⟨2,-5,4⟩=20.$

activity_context.topic_title: The Shortest Distance Between a Plane and a Point

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Shortest Distance Between a Point and a Plane Given in Simplified Dot Product Form
examples.problem: Given that $Q(1,-2,-1)$ lies on the plane $\Pi:\mathbf{r} \cdot \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle = 4,$ find the shortest distance from $P(0 , -1 , 2)$ to $\Pi.$
examples.worked_solution:
First, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =⟨1,-2,-1⟩-⟨0,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

From the equation of a plane, we get a normal vector $\mathbf{n}= \langle 2, 0, -2 \rangle.$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $\Pi$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 0+(-3)\cdot (-2)|}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|2+0+6|}{\sqrt{4+0+4}} \\  & =\frac{|\,8\,|}{\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem: Find the shortest distance between the point $P(1,2,-3)$ and the plane $Π$ with equation $(r-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}])\cdot [\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's pick a point on the plane, for instance, $Q(1,-2,1).$ Then 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -4 \\ 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Also, from the equation of the plane, we get a normal vector $n=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Finally, the shortest distance from the point $P$ to the plane $Π$ is the absolute value of the scalar projection of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ onto the normal vector of the plane:

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|{\text{comp}}_{n}\,\overset{\to }{PQ}| \\  & =\frac{|\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot n|}{|n|} \\  & =\frac{|0\cdot (-2)+(-4)\cdot 1+4\cdot 2|}{\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{|-4+8|}{\sqrt{4+1+4}} \\  & =\frac{|4|}{\sqrt{9}} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
